technical_acceptance_criteria.evidence: Manifest validation requires three distinct conditioning styles, four distinct prompt/operation scenarios, and two distinct seeds. Tests confirm 24 unique case identities and request digests with one output request per case.

The versioned benchmark ledger atomically freezes run identity, all case requests, canonical digests, operation intent, and stable keys before service submission. Changed execution identity blocks new admission; the GenerationService schema is unchanged.

A deterministic termination test stops after service acceptance and resumes by the persisted key, verifies the original digest and job/request IDs, and confirms no duplicate job is created, even when current execution configuration is unavailable.

Resume reconciles persisted jobs before checking whether new execution is allowed. SQLite claims fence competing runners, stale claim epochs cannot update cases, and a deliberately new run receives fresh service-generated request and job identities.

New submissions and queued continuations reach GenerationService only after fixture preflight, compatible frozen execution identity, and service-path checks; GenerationService retains current privacy, capability, adapter, admission, and attempt-budget gates. Selected component identity is checked by ID, role, SHA-256, precision, and quantization. Required roles are validated for every operation declared by the candidate; absent operations remain counted for explicit unsupported outcomes.

The protocol creates separately counted capability, edit, regeneration, chain, composition, and outfit cases and preserves ordered conditioning inputs and chain steps. No live pinned APEX outputs are available to evaluate those supplementary results or chain identity drift.

Preview and final are separate experimental requests with pairing and creative-origin relations distinct from conditioning inputs. No live APEX pair artifacts are available to inspect composition or identity differences.

Reports preserve all 24 matrix denominator slots and distinguish retrieval, benchmark outcome, reconciled service execution, and artifact integrity. Summary status counts follow benchmark_status, while matrix_execution derives completeness and success from service_execution_status. Read-only artifact checks do not create a missing service database or persist integrity observations. A fully executed deterministic CPU matrix remains separate from unverified APEX execution and qualification.

Demonstrated on Python 3.14.4: the focused deterministic CPU-only screening suite passed 50 tests, and the full PR-head make check passed 2166 tests with 5 skips in both paired runs. Coverage includes manifest and candidate validation, fresh and repeat runs, durable claims/recovery after interruption and lost acknowledgment, duplicate invocation, changed fingerprint blocking, unsupported operations/capabilities, service admission/recovery, and complete report accounting. Representative nodes and the full suite were also compared against base. Historical local failures are preserved in commands_run/tests and remain an unresolved baseline reliability followup; they do not negate the deterministic TAC-9 test coverage demonstrated here.

The architecture guide documents report retrieval status, all 24 denominator slots, separate benchmark and service execution counts, read-only artifact inspection, report CLI success, and the unverified APEX execution and qualification boundary.
